items.stem: Starting with unstable zinc (nucleon number 62, proton number 30) in a copper-62 generator positron-decay sequence, purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ) yield a nucleus of A = 62 and Z = 28. What is the signed net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the sequence?
items.workedSolution: Initial neutron number N₀ = 62 − 30 = 32; final neutron number N_f = 62 − 28 = 34. Thus ΔN = N_f − N₀ = 2.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N = A − Z to obtain ΔN = (62 − 28) − (62 − 30) = 2 (B).

items.stem: During a reactor-produced medical generator sequence, weak quark-flavour transitions (one alpha emission and weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ)) convert a parent molybdenum nucleus with A = 99, Z = 42 into a product nucleus with A = 95, Z = 42. How many individual quark-level d → u weak beta transitions occur between the parent and final nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Each weak beta step flips exactly one quark inside a nucleon, changing Z by +1 while keeping A constant. Accounting for ΔA = -4 gives 2 weak quark transitions.

markScheme.criterion: Balances A and Z to identify 2 single-quark weak beta transitions (C).

items.stem: Standard-Model weak-interaction analysis of a fission-product beta-decay cascade links parent strontium (A = 90, Z = 38) to daughter (A = 86, Z = 38) through one alpha emission and weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ). What is the signed net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the sequence?
items.workedSolution: Initial neutron number N₀ = 90 − 38 = 52; final neutron number N_f = 86 − 38 = 48. Thus ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −4.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N = A − Z to obtain ΔN = (86 − 38) − (90 − 38) = −4 (A).

items.stem: Data from a doubly magic heavy-nucleus stability study give the bare nuclear rest mass of lead-208 (nucleon number A = 208, proton number Z = 82) as 207.93163 u. Take free proton mass mₚ = 1.007276 u, free neutron mass mₙ = 1.008665 u, and atomic mass energy equivalent u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this lead-208 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 208 − 82 = 126. Mass defect Δm = 82(1.007276) + 126(1.008665) − 207.93163 = 1.76 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 1.64 × 10³ MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 1.64 × 10³ / 208 = 7.87 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 1.76 u, B = 1.64 × 10³ MeV, and B / A = 7.87 MeV (C).

items.stem: Precision ion-trap records from a neutron-capture control-rod mass evaluation report a bare boron-10 nuclear mass of 10.010194 u for A = 10 and Z = 5. items.stem: Data from a shell-closure nuclear binding survey give the bare nuclear rest mass of calcium-40 (nucleon number A = 40, proton number Z = 20) as 39.951619 u. Take free proton mass mₚ = 1.007276 u, free neutron mass mₙ = 1.008665 u, and atomic mass energy equivalent u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this calcium-40 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 40 − 20 = 20. Mass defect Δm = 20(1.007276) + 20(1.008665) − 39.951619 = 0.367 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 342 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 342 / 40 = 8.55 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.367 u, B = 342 MeV, and B / A = 8.55 MeV (D).

items.stem: Within an iron-group isochronous storage-ring scan, mass spectrometry determines the bare nickel-58 nucleus (A = 58, Z = 28) rest mass to be 57.919996 u; use mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this nickel-58 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 58 − 28 = 30. Mass defect Δm = 28(1.007276) + 30(1.008665) − 57.919996 = 0.544 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 506 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 506 / 58 = 8.73 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.544 u, B = 506 MeV, and B / A = 8.73 MeV (A).

items.stem: Evaluating strong-force binding in a medium-mass storage-ring Schottky scan, a fully stripped silver-107 nucleus (proton number Z = 47, nucleon number A = 107) has rest mass 106.879289 u. Constants: mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this silver-107 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 107 − 47 = 60. Mass defect Δm = 47(1.007276) + 60(1.008665) − 106.879289 = 0.983 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 915 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 915 / 107 = 8.55 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.983 u, B = 915 MeV, and B / A = 8.55 MeV (B).

items.stem: Precision ion-trap records from a heavy-ion storage-ring mass measurement report a bare gold-197 nuclear mass of 196.92323 u for A = 197 and Z = 79. Take mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this gold-197 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 197 − 79 = 118. Mass defect Δm = 79(1.007276) + 118(1.008665) − 196.92323 = 1.67 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 1.56 × 10³ MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 1.56 × 10³ / 197 = 7.92 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 1.67 u, B = 1.56 × 10³ MeV, and B / A = 7.92 MeV (B).

items.stem: To benchmark nuclear stability in a fissile actinide mass-defect determination, consider a bare uranium-235 nucleus of nucleon number A = 235, proton number Z = 92, and nuclear mass 234.99345 u (mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²). What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this uranium-235 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 235 − 92 = 143. Mass defect Δm = 92(1.007276) + 143(1.008665) − 234.99345 = 1.92 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 1.78 × 10³ MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 1.78 × 10³ / 235 = 7.59 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 1.92 u, B = 1.78 × 10³ MeV, and B / A = 7.59 MeV (C).

items.stem: A nuclear data benchmark for a blanket-breeding fusion energetics calculation specifies lithium-6 nucleus (6.013477 u) + deuteron (2.013553 u) → 2 alpha particles (each of mass 4.001506 u) (with mass-energy equivalent u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What is the rest-mass decrease Δm, in atomic mass units (u), in a single fusion reaction?
items.workedSolution: Summing reactant and product rest masses gives Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0240 u.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0240 u (C).

items.stem: Within a pressurized-water thermal fission reactor fuel pin, nuclear power output originates from uranium nucleus (234.99345 u) + 1 thermal neutron (1.008665 u) → barium-141 nucleus (140.88354 u) + krypton-92 nucleus (91.90645 u) + 3 neutrons (each 1.008665 u). Constants: u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fission event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.186 u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 173 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.186 u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 173 MeV (B).

items.stem: Reaction kinematics in a research-reactor fission calorimetry cell examine tellurium–zirconium thermal fission of U-235, where bare rest masses satisfy uranium nucleus (234.99345 u) + 1 thermal neutron (1.008665 u) → tellurium-137 nucleus (136.8986 u) + zirconium-97 nucleus (96.8909 u) + 2 neutrons (each 1.008665 u). Assume 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the rest-mass decrease Δm, in atomic mass units (u), in a single fission reaction?
items.workedSolution: Summing reactant and product rest masses gives Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.195 u.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.195 u (C).

items.stem: Calorimetric analysis of a blanket-breeding fusion energetics calculation evaluates the single-event nuclear fusion step lithium-6 nucleus (6.013477 u) + deuteron (2.013553 u) → 2 alpha particles (each of mass 4.001506 u) (take u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fusion event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0240 u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 22.4 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.0240 u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 22.4 MeV (B).

items.stem: Electrostatic repulsion inside a Geiger–Marsden evacuated scattering chamber halts a head-on alpha particle (charge +2e) of initial energy 5.1 MeV at closest approach d from a stationary gold nucleus (Z = 79, A = 197). Assume k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.1 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(79e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(79)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ = 44.6 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 44.6 fm (C).

items.stem: A collimated proton (charge +1e) carrying 5.7 MeV of kinetic energy undergoes direct head-on Coulomb backscattering from a stationary silver nucleus (Z = 47, A = 107) inside a silicon-diode nuclear recoil goniometer. Constants: k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.7 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(1e)(47e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(1)(47)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ = 11.9 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 11.9 fm (B).

items.stem: Inside an isotopic metallic-foil scattering apparatus, a 5.4 MeV proton (charge +1e) comes momentarily to rest at minimum separation d before reversing direction in front of a tin nucleus (Z = 50, A = 120). Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.4 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.64 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(1e)(50e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(1)(50)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 8.64 × 10⁻¹³ = 13.3 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 13.3 fm (D).

items.stem: To probe the nuclear charge barrier in a nuclear-charge verification scattering cell, a 6.1 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) is fired head-on at a heavy bismuth nucleus (Z = 83, A = 209) with negligible recoil (k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 6.1 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.76 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(83e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(83)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 9.76 × 10⁻¹³ = 39.1 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 39.1 fm (B).

items.stem: Electrostatic repulsion inside a heavy-metal beam-diagnostics scattering foil halts a head-on proton (charge +1e) of initial energy 5.1 MeV at closest approach d from a stationary tantalum nucleus (Z = 73, A = 181). Assume k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.1 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(1e)(73e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(1)(73)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ = 20.6 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 20.6 fm (D).

items.stem: During an experiment in an actinide-target Coulomb turning-point experiment, a alpha particle (charge +2e) of kinetic energy 5.7 MeV is directed along a head-on trajectory toward a fixed thorium nucleus (proton number Z = 90, nucleon number A = 232). Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.7 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(90e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(90)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ = 45.4 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 45.4 fm (D).

items.stem: Elastic 180° backscattering in a Geiger–Marsden evacuated scattering chamber sends a 6.9 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) directly toward an immobile gold target nucleus (Z = 79, A = 197), taking k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 6.9 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.10 × 10⁻¹² J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(79e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(79)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 1.10 × 10⁻¹² = 32.9 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 32.9 fm (A).

What is the estimated nuclear radius R, in femtometres (fm), of the tin-120 nucleus?

items.stem: During an exact cube-root nuclear radius benchmark, a 6.5 MeV alpha beam (charge +2e) probes tellurium-125 nuclei (Z = 52, A = 125). Assume a uniform spherical nucleus obeying R = R₀ A^(1/3), where R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this tellurium-125 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: Nuclear geometry measurements in a refractory tantalum target scattering study direct 7.1 MeV alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) onto tantalum-181 (proton number Z = 73, mass number A = 181), using R = R₀ A^(1/3), R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this tantalum-181 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (C).

What is the estimated nuclear radius R, in femtometres (fm), of the tungsten-184 nucleus?

items.stem: During an electron-scattering nuclear form-factor study, a 4.6 MeV alpha beam (charge +2e) probes carbon-12 nuclei (Z = 6, A = 12). Assume a uniform spherical nucleus obeying R = R₀ A^(1/3), where R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this carbon-12 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: Nuclear geometry measurements in a semiconductor-wafer ion-scattering measurement direct 5.3 MeV alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) onto silicon-28 (proton number Z = 14, mass number A = 28), using R = R₀ A^(1/3), R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this silicon-28 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (A).

items.stem: Within an Earth mountain observatory, atmospheric cosmic-ray muons maintain speed v = 0.96c across a vertical atmospheric column whose proper length is L₀ = 6340 m; their muon rest-frame mean lifetime is Δt₀ = 2.9 × 10⁻⁶ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.96²) = 3.57. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 6340 / 3.57 = 1.78 × 10³ m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 3.57 and L = L₀ / γ = 1.78 × 10³ m (D).

items.stem: Within solar-system navigation buoys, an automated laser-sail nanoprobe maintain speed v = 0.6c across a laser-ranging buoy baseline whose proper length is L₀ = 1.12 × 10⁹ m; their onboard optical-clock tick interval is Δt₀ = 5.58 s. What dilated time interval Δt corresponds to Δt₀ in the stationary observer frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.6²) = 1.25. Dilated time interval Δt = γ Δt₀ = 1.25 × 5.58 = 6.97 s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1.25 and Δt = γ Δt₀ = 6.97 s (D).

items.stem: In the detector cavern, a straight spectrometer flight path has rest length L₀ = 35.5 m. Passing relativistic kaons in a collider arm move parallel to it at v = 0.9c and have a kaon rest-frame proper decay time of Δt₀ = 1.84 × 10⁻⁸ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.9²) = 2.29. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 35.5 / 2.29 = 15.5 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 2.29 and L = L₀ / γ = 15.5 m (B).

items.stem: In a fragment-separator hall, an evacuated time-of-flight beamline has rest length L₀ = 294 m. Passing fast radioactive beryllium-11 nuclei move parallel to it at v = 0.76c and have a nuclear rest-frame proper window of Δt₀ = 1.19 × 10⁻⁶ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.76²) = 1.54. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 294 / 1.54 = 191 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1.54 and L = L₀ / γ = 191 m (A).

items.stem: In a pulsar-wind nebula relativistic shock front, observer frame S′ (post-shock flow S′) travels at v = 0.49c relative to inertial frame S. Simultaneously, upstream energetic positron stream has collinear velocity u = 0.87c in frame S, as depicted on the spacetime diagram. What is the angle θ, in degrees, between the ct′ axis of frame S′ and the ct axis of frame S on the Minkowski diagram?
items.workedSolution: On a Minkowski diagram with axes x and ct, tan θ = |v| / c = 0.49, so θ = arctan(0.49) = 26.1 °.

markScheme.criterion: Uses tan θ = v / c to obtain θ = 26.1 ° (A).

items.workedSolution: On a Minkowski diagram with axes x and ct, tan θ = |v| / c = 0.71, so θ = arctan(0.71) = 35.4 °.

markScheme.criterion: Uses tan θ = v / c to obtain θ = 35.4 ° (D).

items.stem: Observations of a solar-flare coronal magnetic loop detect continuum photoionization edges from six-times ionized nitrogen N⁶⁺ (Z = 7) in excited shell n = 2, where discrete levels satisfy Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (7)² / (2)² = −167 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 167 eV. Final answer: 167 eV. (b) ΔE = 167 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 0.00 J. f = ΔE / h = 0.00 / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 4.02 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 4.02 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (4.02 × 10¹⁶) = 7.46 nm. Final answer: 7.46 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 167 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 4.02 × 10¹⁶ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 7.46 nm.

items.stem: In a young supernova-remnant shock front, seven-times ionized oxygen O⁷⁺ (Z = 8) obeys the Bohr hydrogenic energy relation Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. An electron currently occupies excited shell n = 4. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (8)² / (4)² = −54.4 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 54.4 eV. Final answer: 54.4 eV. (b) ΔE = 54.4 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 0.00 J. f = ΔE / h = 0.00 / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 1.31 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 1.31 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (1.31 × 10¹⁶) = 22.9 nm. Final answer: 22.9 nm.

items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (3)² / (5)² = −4.90 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 4.90 eV. Final answer: 4.90 eV. (b) ΔE = 4.90 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 0.00 J. f = ΔE / h = 0.00 / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 1.18 × 10¹⁵ Hz. Final answer: 1.18 × 10¹⁵ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (1.18 × 10¹⁵) = 254 nm. Final answer: 254 nm.

items.stem: In an X-ray binary accretion-disc corona, five-times ionized carbon C⁵⁺ (Z = 6) obeys the Bohr hydrogenic energy relation Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. An electron currently occupies excited shell n = 2. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (6)² / (2)² = −122 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 122 eV. Final answer: 122 eV. (b) ΔE = 122 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 0.00 J. f = ΔE / h = 0.00 / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 2.95 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 2.95 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (2.95 × 10¹⁶) = 10.2 nm. Final answer: 10.2 nm.

items.workedSolution: (a) ΔZ = 56 − 54 = 2. Final answer: 2. (b) N₀ = 140 − 54 = 86; N_f = 136 − 56 = 80. ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −6. Final answer: −6. (c) Accounting for ΔA = -4, charge conservation gives 4 weak beta transitions. Final answer: 4.

State the nuclear radius R in metres.
Taking the mass of the nucleus to be A u, calculate the mean nuclear density ρ in kg m⁻³.

items.stem: In a closed-proton-shell tin scattering run, alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) of kinetic energy 6.5 MeV scatter from a spherical tin-120 target nucleus with proton number Z = 50 and nucleon number A = 120. Model the nuclear radius as R = R₀ A^(1/3) with R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and nucleon mass unit u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
items.workedSolution: (a) R = 1.20 × (120)^(1/3) = 5.92 fm. Final answer: 5.92 fm. (b) R = 5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Final answer: 5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. (c) m = 120 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; V = (4/3)π(5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵)³. ρ = m / V = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

Divides nuclear mass A u by spherical volume (4/3)πR³.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Worldlines plotted on a Minkowski diagram for a cosmic-ray air-shower Lorentz boost analysis assign velocity v = 0.84c to secondary pion frame S′ and velocity u = 0.97c to forward decay muon, both measured in frame S.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1 / √(1 − v²/c²).

Applies u′ = (u − v) / (1 − uv/c²) preserving algebraic signs.
Evaluates correctly to 0.702.
